flags: A biased die can still happen to have P(6) = 1/6 while other face probabilities differ. B rejects the counting justification, not the numerical possibility.
The answer rejects an unjustified equal-outcome counting argument. Bias does not itself prove that the probability of face 6 differs from 1/6.

question: A biased die is rolled. Can 1/6 be used as the probability of rolling a 6? Why?
solution: The value 1/6 is calculated using \(P=m/n\), which requires all outcomes to be equally likely. When the die is biased, the scores are not equally likely, so 1/6 cannot be used directly.
